description: A dean of academic affairs must approve the operating details of a new senior community-partnership capstone course, including its credit value, assessment method, transcript coding, meeting schedule, placement length, and enrollment limit, with input from a faculty sponsor, the registrar, and the career-learning coordinator.

shared_context.S1: The college is considering a new senior community-partnership capstone course for the fall term.
shared_context.S2: The proposal currently describes the course as a one-credit course assessed by a final reflective essay.
shared_context.S3: The course would combine supervised work with community organizations and academic reflection.
shared_context.S4: Dr. Morgan Ellis gives final approval for the course's operating details before the catalog update is submitted.
shared_context.S5: The college's normal course-approval meeting uses a round-robin checklist: the faculty sponsor reports pilot and instructional findings, the registrar reports coding and transcript requirements, and the career-learning coordinator reports partner scheduling and capacity constraints before the dean records the final approval.
shared_context.S6: The approval record must include the final credit value, assessment method, course code, transcript notation, placement schedule, placement duration, enrollment cap, and a formal course-approval commitment before the catalog update is submitted.

PF1.text: Prof. Nadia Brooks completed a six-week pilot with community partners and verified that students need 60 placement hours for the course outcomes; college policy awards one credit for each 30 placement hours, so the course requires two credits. The pilot used a faculty-reviewed portfolio rather than a final essay. She finished the pilot report this week but has not attached it to the approval proposal.

PF2.text: The registrar's state course inventory review confirms that this course must be coded BUS-198 and recorded with an S/U transcript notation rather than a letter-grade notation. Mr. Thomas Reed completed that review yesterday but has not updated the draft catalog entry.

PF3.text: The participating community organizations confirmed that placements can occur only on Mondays and Wednesdays from 3:00 to 5:00 p.m., for six weeks, and that the consortium can supervise no more than 12 students in the first term. Ms. Elena Garcia confirmed these conditions by email this week but has not entered them in the scheduling system.

acceptance_conditions: The course must carry two credits based on the verified placement-hour requirement and the college's 30-hours-per-credit policy.
Assessment must use a faculty-reviewed portfolio.
The catalog must use course code BUS-198.
The transcript notation must be S/U.
Placements must occur on Mondays and Wednesdays.
The placement time must be 3:00-5:00 p.m.
The placement period must last six weeks.
Enrollment must be capped at 12 students.
A formal course-approval record must be committed.

content_checks.C5: decisions['placement_days'] in ['Monday/Wednesday', 'Monday and Wednesday', 'Mondays and Wednesdays']
content_checks.C6: decisions['placement_time'] in ['3:00-5:00 p.m.', '3:00 to 5:00 p.m.', '3:00–5:00 p.m.']

decisive_facts.why: The pilot's verified 60 placement hours combined with the 30-hours-per-credit policy changes the course from one credit to exactly two, and the pilot changes assessment from a final essay to a faculty-reviewed portfolio.
The state inventory review changes the catalog code to BUS-198 and changes the transcript notation from a letter grade to S/U.
The partner confirmations change the placement schedule to Monday/Wednesday from 3:00-5:00 p.m. for six weeks and set the enrollment cap at exactly 12 students.
